author: agent
text:
MEASURED ON REAL REPOS 2026-08-22, immediately after shipping. Two things worth knowing before changing this.

THE PAYLOAD BUG, and it is the reason MEMBERS_CAP exists. The first version bounded GROUPS at twelve and let each group carry every member. On pytest@df87db7 that returned 12 groups holding 193 member rows - 36,433 characters, roughly 9,000 tokens for one call - and nothing in the payload said a list had been cut, because none had. The rule was applied at the top level and forgotten one level down. payload.py's docstring names exactly this shape and this is the seventh instance of it in this codebase. Bounding both levels took it to 12,424 characters, a 66 percent cut, with members_shown and members_total on every group.

WHAT THE RESULTS ACTUALLY LOOK LIKE ON REAL CODE, so nobody mistakes it for a defect. The top groups on pytest and pydantic are dominated by TEST entities - 27 structurally identical test bodies, 20 three-line validators inside one dataclass test. That is true duplication and the hash is right, but it is not what a reader means by "where does my repo repeat itself". On memway's own map the largest group is the genuine finding: one 3-line subprocess helper copied into seven test files under two names, which is worth fixing.

So the signal is honest and the RANKING is by group size, which on a test-heavy repo puts parametrized tests first. If this is ever tuned, the fix is a production/test split reported as a fact - is_test_entity already exists and is the one rule for it - not a filter that silently drops entities, and not a floor raised until the noise disappears. Raising min_loc was tried during design and discards the true positives before the noise: at loc>=5 memway's own _cli and _git groups vanish and only 3 groups survive.

THE NEAR TIER IS CORRECT AND SLOW-LOOKING BUT IS NOT. It is O(n) sketch comparisons against every eligible entity - 6,699 on pydantic - and completes in 0.4s because the sketch is 48 packed integers. Verified end to end rather than assumed: model_dump's best neighbour is model_dump_json at 0.646, which is semantically the right answer, and a threshold of 0.8 correctly returns nothing. A zero from this tier is a real zero, not a silent failure - checked by confirming the sketch was populated (48 values, 483 shingles) before believing the empty result.
